correctness.rationale: For K=H−iΓ the dark space is the orthogonal sum of the H-eigenspace kernels of the site evaluations. It reduces K because H preserves it and Γ annihilates it. The imaginary-part eigenvalue identity leaves no real eigenvalue on its complement, so the latter decays even if K is defective. The surviving weight is therefore tr(P_dark ρ), and the bright rank adds the separate evaluation ranks. In the hub/uniform block the roots are 1±√(1+ng²); the upper root exceeds 2 and the lower one encounters each distinct negative nonuniform rim energy exactly once. Every bare rim eigenspace has a vector nonzero at the sink, so merging loses exactly one rank, and adding the hub evaluation gives rank two on the merged eigenspace. At a collision write a=ng² and M=a+λ². With only the rim sink, the bright vector of the merged energy is the spectral projection of the rim site. Its squared norm is (λ²/M+d)/n; the hub's squared overlap with its normalized direction is (a/M)λ²/(λ²+dM). Subtraction from the hub's weight a/M in this eigenspace gives da/(da+(d+1)λ²). The other hybrid level is fully captured. The exact boundary checks include n=3 (λ=−1,d=2,S_h=2/3) and the even singleton at n=4 (λ=−2,d=1,S_h=1/2); a zero rim energy never collides for g>0. For n≥5 the first negative rim mode has d=2 and ε=−λ≤4π/n, giving 1−S_h=3ε/(4+5ε)≤3π/n and g²=ε(2+ε)/n. The discontinuity is only in the eventual limit. The frozen NumPy checker groups numerical eigenspaces at absolute tolerance 2e−8 for n=3,…,30; I inspected its scope and recorded results, not executed it. Exact claims follow from the independent spectral argument, not the bounded sample.

value.rationale: A complete one- and two-sink classification for this weighted network shows how exact degeneracy can protect an excitation initially adjacent to a lossy site even though arbitrary detuning eventually captures it. The explicit survival probability, rate independence, and the sequence approaching unit protection give usable quantitative content beyond listing level crossings; the result does not imply robustness to detuning or finite-time discontinuity.
